# Kneading vs Folding

Kneading and folding both develop gluten; they differ in how much strength
they build per minute and how much gas they press back out of a dough on the
way. A baker chooses between them by asking what the dough still needs, not
by habit.^[raw/articles/the-science-of-a-good-loaf.md]

## Where they differ

- Kneading works the dough hard and continuously, building strength fast in
  a dough that has not yet rested.
- Folding turns a dough in its container a few times over hours, adding
  strength gently while keeping most of the gas it has already caught.
- A dough that has rested long may need only a few folds, while a dough
  mixed and shaped straight away needs real kneading.
